cell.condition_text: Wisconsin statutes shown define 'lobbyist' by employment/contract for economic consideration (other than reimbursement for actual expenses) and a 5-days-per-reporting-period communication test when duties are not exclusively lobbying; no dollar-amount compensation threshold is specified.

instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.62(11) defines who is a 'lobbyist' without setting any minimum compensation dollar figure, instead using receipt of economic consideration and (in mixed-duty cases) a 5-day lobbying-communications threshold.

cell.condition_text: Applies to principal expense statements: if payments/obligations to any one lobbyist exceed $200 in a reporting period, the principal must list the lobbyist’s name/address and total amount paid/owed.

instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.68(1)(a)6 requires itemization (name/address and total) only when lobbying expenditures/obligations to a specific lobbyist exceed $200 during the reporting period.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled text contains no lobbyist-definition or licensure threshold based on a lobbyist’s own lobbying expenditures; only principal registration and principal expense-reporting thresholds are provided (e.g., §§ 13.64, 13.68).

The bundled text imposes expense-statement filing duties on registered principals (Wis. Stat. § 13.68) and provides a principal-side $500 verified-statement exemption (Wis. Stat. § 13.621(5)), but it does not contain a lobbyist-side de minimis dollar threshold exempting lobbyists from disclosure filing.

No statute in the bundle creates a lobbyist’s own time-percentage exemption from filing disclosures; the only quantified time carveouts shown are principal-reporting exclusions for certain employees (e.g., non-lobbyist employees devoting ≤10 hours per reporting period) in Wis. Stat. § 13.68(1).

arguments.condition_text: Wisconsin defines 'lobbyist' using a 5-days-with-lobbying-communications test (when duties are not exclusively lobbying), not a percentage-of-time threshold.
arguments.justification: Section 13.62(11) uses a '5 days within a reporting period' standard for mixed-duty individuals and does not provide any percent-of-time trigger for being a lobbyist.
